card.band: 4 h. A mid-size surface with many options. A frontier agent covers the download path and misses the restore-key semantics, safe path handling and range retries. A weaker model stops at a single-key download.
card.cheat: The feature is not in upstream, so there is nothing to copy. The mock service's behaviours are hidden and probed with unseen keys and archives.
card.grading: Hidden Go tests through the cobra command tree, with httpmock-style fixtures and generated tarballs (about 250 scenarios). The existing suite is a regression gate. Credit is the fraction passed.
card.reference: Our implementation, estimated at 1200-1800 lines including cmd packages, API client changes and tests.
card.task: /app ships a pinned gh snapshot and a mock Actions cache HTTP service. The agent adds `gh cache download` and `gh cache restore`: key and ref selection, restore-key prefix matching, chunked download, zstd/tar unpack, checksum verification, `--json` output and a cross-ref filter, with help and error handling. It adds tests, and also covers listing filters and pagination as needed.

facts.claim: cli/cli issue #9125 exists, is open, opened 2024-05-24, and requests a `gh cache download` subcommand for Actions caches
Issue #9125 has no linked branches or pull requests; comments describe only workarounds, not a CLI implementation
Maintainers say the Actions cache REST APIs only support list, view and delete, with no GraphQL objects, and the request was escalated to the Actions team (blocked label)
pkg/cmd/cache on trunk contains only delete, list, shared and cache.go, with no download or restore subcommand
gh release v2.102.0 exists (released 30 Sep; year not shown on page)
The v2.102.0 changelog has no entry mentioning gh cache, download or restore
The cli/cli repository is licensed under the MIT License (Copyright (c) 2019 GitHub Inc.)
The public GitHub REST Actions cache API has no endpoint that downloads a cache archive (only list, get, delete, usage and limits)
The pinned head 5cfe3062 is the commit the smoke build ran on

Band.why: 4 h tier fits a mid-size surface, but no dated public evidence, so capped at 3; weaker model stopping at single-key is a real gap

Build.why: Estimated 3-4 days; smoke probe red/amber with timeouts

Fit.why: Go on 8 cores is fine, but offline build and suite timing were not proven by the probe

Hor.why: 4 h is fitting for the scope, but the surface is closer to a few-thousand-line sweep than a deep multi-week task

Multi.why: Many independent buckets: key/ref, restore-keys, chunking, unpack, checksum, json, filter, pagination

Real.why: Real open gh issue #9125 and MIT repo; the download protocol itself is a mock, not a real API, since public REST has no archive download

Ref.why: Own reference not written yet; complete permissive gh implementation is plausible but will be tied to an invented mock protocol

Seal.why: Hidden mock instance and cases are sealable, but a shipped mock is readable and the actions/cache wire format is recallable

Surf.why: About 250 hidden scenarios through cobra with generated tarballs and mock behaviours

spike_plan.kill_if: The offline build cannot be made to succeed with a pre-filled module cache, or the existing suite cannot be pruned to a stable regression gate (failures vary between runs without a clear cause).
spike_plan.pass_if: Offline build of ./cmd/gh succeeds with a pre-filled module cache in under about 15 min; the cache-package tests are stable across 3 runs; the stub download works end-to-end against the local mock.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone cli/cli and check out v2.102.0 (confirm the head is 5cfe3062; the smoke probe ran ad27e286, so re-pin).
Run `go mod download`, then time `go build ./cmd/gh` and record the module cache size. This tests whether the offline GOPROXY=off build fits the budget.

Run `go test -json ./pkg/cmd/cache/...` and then `go test -json -p 4 ./...` twice. Compare failures with the probe's 3004 flaky count and the 8 stable failures to see if the existing suite can serve as a regression gate.

Write a 60-line throwaway mock cache server (list and download routes, one archive) and a stub `gh cache download <key>` that calls it. Check one end-to-end run with GOPROXY=off after the module cache is filled.
Run one fixed new test three times to check determinism, and confirm the mock wire format is independent of the public actions/cache npm protocol.

v1.summary: The seed is real and not in upstream: cli/cli #9125 is open with no PR, and the v2.102.0 release and MIT licence check out. It is not killed, but it is conditional: the smoke probe was amber/red at a different commit (ad27e286 vs 5cfe3062), the public REST API has no archive download so the protocol is a mock, and the build is unproven offline, so the spike must confirm the offline build and a stable regression gate before the 4 h tier is trusted.

v2.note: Maintainers confirm no public API exists for downloading caches, so the mock wire format and restore semantics would be our invention. That leaves no real artifact to test against, and a hand-written scenario suite would encode our own design choices. Infrastructure is also shaky: the smoke build timed out on every step, it reported 3004 flaky tests, and the pinned head contradicts the commit that was probed.
